---
title: "PIT_PS: Payment Summaries"
description: "Information from payment summaries provided by employers to their employees and submitted to the ATO, including payments and the amounts withheld from those payments."
---

Information from payment summaries provided by employers to their employees and submitted to the ATO, including payments and the amounts withheld from those payments.

*Describes payment-summary income, withholding information, coverage and limitations.*

Tax records keep changing after the income year closes, as returns are lodged late, amended and audited, so the same income year extracted at two dates is two different datasets. The suffix on the table name is that lag: ato_pay_sum_2223_12m is the 2022-23 year as it stood twelve months after the year ended. This column is what tells you which vintage you are reading, and comparing across years means comparing like lags rather than like income years.","dsrc":"ABS administrative income sources","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/concepts-sources-methods/administrative-income-comparison-studies/2019-20-2021","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"ATO data extract time","k":"ATO extract reference date","def":"The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.","p":"2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS administrative income sources","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/concepts-sources-methods/administrative-income-comparison-studies/2019-20-2021","lim":"The column describes the extract, not the person, so it is never an analysis variable. An early extract understates a year's income because late lodgers are missing, and the shortfall is not spread evenly: it falls on people with complex affairs and on those who lodge through an agent. It is the outer frame for the row, while the income year column repeats the year written on the form and the period dates say how much of that year the payments span. Its value earns its keep once several year tables are stacked, because it is what the stacked rows are ordered by.","dsrc":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/about/data-services/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Reference financial year","k":"Australian financial year of the extract (1 July to 30 June)","def":"A financial year label rather than a date. The ATO defines the label as \"all salary, wages, bonuses and commissions you paid your payee as an employee, company director or office holder\" and adds \"Include the total gross amount before amounts are withheld\". It excludes anything shown in its own column, because employers are told not to include allowances, lump sums, CDEP payments or reportable fringe benefits here.","dsrc":"ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/payg-payment-summary-individual-non-business/section-b-payment-details","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Gross payment amount","k":"Dollar amount at the gross payments label","def":"A whole-dollar amount, gross of tax withheld. Lump sum A is unused leave paid out when someone leaves a job, and the ATO splits it in two: code R covers unused annual leave, leave loading and post-1978 long service leave paid out for genuine redundancy, invalidity or an early retirement scheme, and code T covers the same kinds of leave paid out for any other reason. R is concessionally taxed and T is not, so the code is the difference between a redundancy and a resignation on an otherwise identical row.","dsrc":"ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines: when an employee transfers or leaves","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/when-an-employee-transfers-or-leaves","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Lump sum a type","k":"ATO lump sum A type code","def":"The ATO's lump sum type code, reported alongside the lump sum A amount. The payment summary instruction limits the label to leave that accrued before that date, and the return then cuts the figure down: the taxpayer adds up the Lump sum B amounts and is told to \"Divide the total by 20. This is because only 5% is taxable.\" The summary therefore shows an amount twenty times larger than the income that reaches the assessment.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 3 Employer lump sum payments","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/3-employer-lump-sum-payments-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Lump sum b","k":"Dollar amount at the Lump sum B label","def":"A whole-dollar gross amount of pre-16 August 1978 long service leave, reported separately from gross payments and from Lump sum A.","p":"2009-2010 to 2022-2023","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 3 Employer lump sum payments","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/3-employer-lump-sum-payments-2025","lim":"The column will not reconcile with the person's return: the return carries five per cent of it, so joining payment summary amounts to assessed income without the divide-by-twenty step overstates income by the difference. Only workers with unbroken service from the 1970s can have any value here, so it is close to empty in the later years and is not a general measure of long service leave.","where":["madip-ge-020101d-ato-atopaysum1011-fy2010-11 / ato_pay_sum_1011","madip-ge-020106d-ato-atopaysum1112-fy2011-12 / ato_pay_sum_1112","madip-ge-020111d-ato-atopaysum1213-fy2012-13 / ato_pay_sum_1213","madip-ge-020116d-ato-atopaysum1314-fy2013-14 / ato_pay_sum_1314","madip-ge-020121d-ato-atopaysum1415-fy2014-15 / ato_pay_sum_1415","madip-ge-020126d-ato-atopaysum1516-fy2015-16 / ato_pay_sum_1516","madip-ge-020131d-ato-atopaysum1617-fy2016-17 / ato_pay_sum_1617","madip-ge-020136d-ato-atopaysum1718-fy2017-18 / ato_pay_sum_1718","madip-ge-020136d-ato-atopaysum1819-fy2018-19 / ato_pay_sum_1819","madipge-ato-d-pay-sum-fy0910 / ato_pay_sum_0910_16m","madipge-ato-d-pay-sum-fy1920 / ato_pay_sum_1920","madipge-ato-d-pay-sum-fy1920 / ato_pay_sum_1920_16m","and 7 more"]},{"n":"LSPD_AMT","d":"The tax-free slice of a genuine redundancy or early retirement scheme payment, which the payee never declares.","full":"The tax-free slice of a genuine redundancy or early retirement scheme payment, which the payee never declares. The ATO defines the label as \"The tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment\", and the return instructions for question 3 tell taxpayers to leave these amounts out because no tax is payable on them. A non-zero value is the clearest redundancy marker on the payment summary.","dsrc":"ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/payg-payment-summary-individual-non-business/section-b-payment-details","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Lump sum d","k":"Dollar amount at the Lump sum D label","def":"A whole-dollar amount capped by the statutory tax-free limit, which depends on completed years of service and is indexed each year. Anything above the tax-free limit becomes an employment termination payment reported on a different form, so a large redundancy can show a modest figure here and the rest elsewhere, and two workers with identical severance show different amounts because their years of service differ. The ATO defines the label as \"Amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments\". The return sends it to a different question from ordinary wages: employer lump sum payments in arrears are declared at question 24 Other income rather than at the salary questions.","dsrc":"ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/payg-payment-summary-individual-non-business/section-b-payment-details","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Lump sum e","k":"Dollar amount at the Lump sum E label","def":"A whole-dollar amount excluded from gross payments, covering salary and wage arrears that accrued more than twelve months before payment.","p":"2009-2010 to 2022-2023","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/payg-payment-summary-individual-non-business/section-b-payment-details","lim":"It does not say which years the arrears belong to or how many, so it cannot be spread back over the years the work was done, and the offset it triggers depends on that spread. The ABS describes mesh blocks as \"the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS\" which \"form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS)\", designed to hold between 30 and 60 dwellings. The SA1 to SA4, LGA and state codes on the same row are this one mesh block aggregated upward.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Mesh Blocks","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/mesh-blocks","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Asgs 2016 meshblock","k":"Mesh block, ASGS main structure","def":"An eleven-digit ASGS mesh block code. The ABS notes that the step carries a risk of its own: \"The impact of any changes made directly to the address information should be evaluated against the unrepaired addresses to ensure the changes do not inadvertently result in incorrect address matching.\" The repairs are formatting fixes, a state added from the postcode and bad characters removed. CONST on the same row names the index the repaired address was then matched against.","dsrc":"Australian Bureau of Statistics, SSF Guidance Material - Geocoding Unit Record Data Using Address and Location, section 'Address repair'","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/statistical-geography/statistical-spatial-framework-ssf/statistical-spatial-framework-guidance-material/ssf-guidance-material-geocoding-unit-record-data-using-address-and-location","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Address repair result","k":"abs_address_repair_result","def":"A short outcome value separating an address the repair step changed, one it examined and left alone, and one that needed nothing. The ATO sets the test as: \"Complete this section if the total taxable value of certain fringe benefits you provided to your payee in the fringe benefits tax (FBT) year (1 April to 31 March) exceeds $2,000 for the FBT year.\" An employee whose benefits fall under the threshold shows nothing here, and an employer eligible for exemption from FBT under section 57A ticks a Yes indicator box beside the amount on the same summary.","dsrc":"ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/payg-payment-summary-individual-non-business/section-b-payment-details","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Reportable fringe benefits amount","k":"Dollar amount at the reportable fringe benefits label (grossed up)","def":"A whole-dollar grossed-up taxable value for the FBT year, reported on the payment summary for the corresponding financial year and excluded from gross payments.","p":"2009-2010 to 2022-2023","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/payg-payment-summary-individual-non-business/section-b-payment-details","lim":"The figure is not the cash value of the benefit, because grossing up inflates it to the pre-tax salary equivalent, so treating it as remuneration in dollars overstates the benefit by the gross-up factor. In the 2015-16 to 2018-19 years it is delivered in a separate geography table keyed to the person rather than inline with the payments.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-1","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 1 (SA1) 2011","k":"Statistical Area Level 1, ASGS main structure","def":"An eleven-digit ASGS code. It is the level most PLIDA analysis settles on, because SA1 is too sparse for annual income measures and SA3 is too coarse for a suburb.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"SA2","k":"Statistical Area Level 2, ASGS main structure","def":"A nine-digit ASGS code, one value per row, with 2,473 areas covering Australia including nineteen non-spatial special purpose codes.","p":"2015-2016 to 2022-2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","lim":"An SA2 is a residence, not a labour market, so wages summed by this column measure where earners sleep rather than where the jobs are; the SA4 code on the same row is the labour market level.
